title: Week Ahead — Market Outlook
headline: A mid-teens VIX masks a catalyst-heavy week in which long-end Treasury supply, Nvidia earnings, PCE data, Jackson Hole and Iran-related energy risk could quickly reprice rates and AI-led equities.
volatilityRationale: The VIX is still in the mid-teens, but it rose from Friday’s close into early Monday trading while the market enters the week with elevated long-bond yields, oil and geopolitical uncertainty. Multiple scheduled catalysts—Nvidia earnings, PCE and income data, Treasury auctions and the Jackson Hole symposium—make a larger-than-usual move plausible even without a disorderly volatility regime.

recap.text: U.S. equities broke a three-week winning streak: Reuters reported weekly declines of 1.43% for the S&P 500, 2.05% for the Nasdaq and 0.85% for the Dow through Friday, with rate sensitivity especially visible in technology shares.

The Treasury’s surprise decision to double planned long-end buybacks briefly eased the bond selloff, but the relief faded as 10- and 30-year yields climbed again, keeping fiscal and inflation concerns at the center of the regime.

Oil rose for a second straight week as the U.S. threatened tougher sanctions on Iran and uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz kept supply risk in focus, adding an inflationary shock channel for rates and equities.

August flash data showed U.S. services activity accelerating while manufacturing slowed, a mix that supports growth but can keep inflation and policy expectations sensitive to energy and wage developments.
The Federal Reserve released the July 28–29 FOMC minutes on August 19, giving investors a fresh read on the policy debate before this week’s Jackson Hole communications.

triggers.text: Treasury bill and coupon-note auctions run through the week; weak demand or a poor auction tail would reinforce the long-end yield pressure that hurt risk assets last week.
Nvidia reports fiscal Q2 2027 results after the close, making the release and guidance a key test of AI-capex expectations and the crowded semiconductor trade.
BEA releases the second estimate of Q2 GDP, corporate profits and July Personal Income and Outlays, including the PCE inflation data watched by the Fed and rates markets.

The Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium runs Aug. 27–29; Chair Kevin Warsh’s keynote remarks are scheduled for Aug. 28, creating a direct risk of repricing in the policy path and long-end term premium.

The Treasury Secretary is scheduled to hold a press conference on Monday after the U.S. warned of additional Iran sanctions and intervened to support long-duration bonds, so policy headlines could move both oil and yields.

watch.text: Watch whether the VIX remains near 16 while credit and equity breadth stay calm; a simultaneous rise in spot volatility and Treasury yields would be a stronger risk-off signal than either move alone.

Track the 10- and 30-year Treasury yield response to auctions and buybacks. A failed follow-through on Treasury support would keep duration, growth stocks and leveraged AI infrastructure financing under pressure.
Follow oil, shipping and sanctions headlines around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz; a renewed supply shock would challenge the soft-landing narrative through inflation expectations.
Use Cboe’s SKEW dashboard alongside VIX to check whether options markets are paying up for tail protection even if headline volatility stays subdued.
